elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to any affiliate.
elements.evidence: The consent carve-out is limited to a “financially responsible affiliate,” rather than any affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Client to assign without approval to a successor in a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Client to assign without approval to a successor in an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Client to assign without approval to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: TrueLink remains subject to the requirement for Client’s prior written approval.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Client’s approval of any assignment or transfer by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly prohibits TrueLink from assigning or transferring its rights to a competitor of Client.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right upon Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that a change of control of Client shall not give TrueLink any right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice when assigning to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor carve-out contains no written-notice requirement.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: TrueLink has no successor carve-out and remains subject to Client’s prior written approval.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice when assigning to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no written-notice mechanism for a TrueLink assignment to a successor.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to Customer's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard applies only to Client’s approval of TrueLink assignments; no equivalent restriction applies to TrueLink’s approval of Client assignments.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Client’s approval of any assignment or transfer by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The redline closely approaches the preferred position but does not permit assignment to every affiliate because it retains the “financially responsible” qualification. It also fails the fallback because successor assignment rights are not mutual, written notice is not required, and only Client’s consent is subject to a reasonableness standard. The changes are otherwise coherent and preserve unrelated terms, but no complete playbook level is achieved.
